stories.title: Framework and Standard Setting: Principles for Agentic Trust
stories.situation: At Sling, non-deterministic AI behavior required a human-factors framework that went beyond conventional deterministic usability checks.
stories.task: Create a rigorous way to audit whether agentic systems deserved user trust and preserved user control.
stories.action: Developed Principles for Agentic Trust around four audit dimensions: Alignment, Execution, Control, and Calibration.
stories.result: The framework was accepted at ACM CSCW 2026 Industry Perspectives.
stories.earned_secret: High trust in non-deterministic AI isn't built by hiding uncertainty; it's built by making system observability explicit during execution.

stories.title: $50M Psychophysics Latency Program and Patent
stories.situation: Amazon Devices used arbitrary engineering latency targets that were not grounded in what people could actually perceive.
stories.task: Translate human perceptual limits into defensible multimodal system requirements at major program scale.
stories.action: Built a psychophysics-led approach to latency thresholds, supported cognitive-load modeling with fNIRS and eye tracking, and contributed multimodal interaction architecture captured in US Patent US-12532040-B1.
stories.result: The work informed a $50M program and replaced arbitrary targets with human perceptual thresholds.
stories.earned_secret: Arbitrary engineering SLAs waste millions; human perceptual thresholds are non-linear, so latency targets must be anchored to cognitive trust degradation curves.

stories.title: Lunar Gateway Clinical Workstation Risk Validation
stories.situation: NASA Langley's Lunar Gateway clinical workstation work involved safety-critical human performance in a constrained spaceflight environment.
stories.task: Validate the Human-Systems Integration design against foreseeable use failures and applicable human-factors standards.
stories.action: Applied use Failure Mode and Effects Analysis alongside NASA-STD-3001 and MIL-STD-1472 guidance to structure validation and risk identification.
stories.result: Produced standards-grounded HSI validation evidence for the clinical workstation effort; specific design changes and risk reductions require candidate confirmation before interview use.
stories.earned_secret: In safety-critical aerospace/clinical environments, task speed isn't the primary safety metric—eliminating high-consequence use-error modes via physical display layout is.
stories.evidence_status: Core work is candidate-supplied; outcome detail needs validation

stories.title: Pushing Back on Frictionless UX
stories.situation: Autonomous defense systems create cases where optimizing every interaction for speed and seamlessness can remove the pause needed for human judgment.
stories.task: Articulate a product and research position that preserves operational tempo without turning the operator into a passive approver.
stories.action: Formulated Calibrated Cognitive Friction: intentional, risk-proportional checkpoints that expose uncertainty, interrupt automation bias, and enforce Meaningful Human Control.
stories.result: Established the central thesis for the Anduril interview; production deployment evidence must not be claimed unless separately validated.
stories.earned_secret: Friction is not inherently a usability defect. At consequential decision boundaries, well-calibrated friction is a control surface that protects human agency and improves the quality of authorization.
stories.evidence_status: Philosophy supplied; operational result not yet evidenced

stories.title: Multimodal Hardware-Software Handover Design
stories.situation: At Amazon Devices and Mercedes-Benz R&D, user performance depended on coordinated physical and digital cues rather than a screen-only interface.
stories.task: Determine how biometric, haptic, auditory, and visual signals should support attention, cognitive load, and control transitions.
stories.action: Used multimodal interaction architecture, simulator studies of Level 2/Level 3 handovers, and biometric methods including fNIRS and eye tracking to study human-system performance.
stories.result: Generated evidence relevant to multimodal architecture and autonomous handovers; Echo Hub-specific outcome details require candidate confirmation.
stories.earned_secret: A handover is not a notification event; it is a time-bounded transfer of situation awareness, confidence, and physical control across modalities.
stories.evidence_status: Methods supplied; product-specific outcome detail needs validation

stories.title: Answering Dr. Kim's Learners Keynote Questions
stories.situation: Dr. Daniella Kim's Learners keynote raises difficult questions at the boundary of autonomous-system performance, human judgment, and research velocity.
stories.task: Turn those open questions into a defensible Human Factors research thesis for Anduril Air Defense.
stories.action: Use Calibrated Cognitive Friction and the Principles for Agentic Trust to frame testable claims, identify biometric and behavioral measures, and connect findings to system and product decisions.
stories.result: Prepared a Lead/Staff-level interview agenda; the exact keynote questions, proposed studies, and any interaction with Dr. Kim must be validated before use.
stories.earned_secret: Lead-level influence does not require pretending an ambiguous question is solved; it requires converting ambiguity into a falsifiable research program whose decision consequences are clear to engineering and product leaders.
stories.evidence_status: Interview preparation hypothesis; requires source validation

stories.title: Mercedes-Benz L2/L3 Autonomous Handover Alerting
stories.situation: At Mercedes-Benz Research & Development, Level 2 and Level 3 autonomy required the driver to resume control on short notice without losing situational awareness.
stories.task: Determine which alert modalities prepare a disengaged driver to take back control safely.
stories.action: Ran high-fidelity simulator studies of Level 2 and Level 3 handovers using biometric, auditory, tactile, and haptic alerts.
stories.result: Improved safety and trust ratings by 24%.
stories.earned_secret: Multimodal alerts (auditory + haptic) reduce handover panic by priming driver situational awareness before control transition.

stories.title: Uber Mobile HMI and Urban Spatial Navigation
stories.primary_skill: Field research under real operational stress
stories.situation: At Uber, drivers used a mobile interface for complex spatial navigation while managing live traffic, passengers, and time pressure.
stories.task: Understand how in-the-moment interface demands affected driver performance and willingness to keep driving.
stories.action: Conducted urban field studies of mobile HMI and complex spatial navigation in real driving conditions rather than in the lab.
stories.result: Contributed to a 5% increase in driver retention.
stories.earned_secret: Information density must dynamically scale down during high-stress maneuvers to prevent visual cognitive overload.

stories.title: Objective Biometric Telemetry for Acute-Stress Workload
stories.situation: At Brigham and Women's Hospital / Harvard Medical School, acute-stress research depended on physiological signal processing rather than self-report, and the candidate's Old Dominion doctoral work studied working memory, spatial processing, and reaction times during high-stress task interruptions.
stories.task: Establish what objective physiological data reveals about cognitive state under acute stress.
stories.action: Processed functional neuroimaging (fMRI), ECG, and telemetry data for acute-stress research, and later built an fNIRS and eye-tracking cognitive load framework at Amazon.
stories.result: Produced an objective measurement foundation for cognitive workload; the specific comparison against subjective survey instruments requires candidate confirmation before interview use.
stories.earned_secret: Objective biometric telemetry (fNIRS/ECG) uncovers cognitive workload spikes that subjective post-task surveys (like NASA-TLX) completely miss.
stories.evidence_status: Methods are candidate-supplied; NASA-TLX comparison and fNIRS use at Brigham are not in the canonical resume and need validation
